theory.intro: The best graph for a dataset depends on the type of data and what you want to show. Match the data and its purpose to the display that shows it most clearly.
steps: Identify the type of data (categorical or numerical).
Identify the purpose (compare categories, show a distribution, show change over time, or show parts of a whole).
Match the data and purpose to the display that shows it best.

workedExamples.question_text:
A library records the number of books borrowed in four categories: fiction, biography, science and history. It wants to compare the actual numbers borrowed.
Choose a suitable graph and justify your choice.
workedExamples.solution_text: A column graph. Book category is categorical data, and separate columns make the actual numbers borrowed easy to compare. A sector graph would emphasise each category’s share of the total.

workedExamples.question_text:
A nursery records a plant’s height at the end of each week for $6$ weeks.
Choose a suitable graph to show how its height changes over time. Explain one advantage of your choice.
workedExamples.solution_text: A line graph. Height is continuous numerical data recorded over time. Joining successive readings shows the change in height and allows estimates between readings.

workedExamples.question_text:
A club records monthly spending on equipment, venue hire and transport.
(a) Choose a suitable graph to show each category’s percentage of the total spending.
(b) Choose a suitable graph to compare the actual amounts spent on the three categories.
Justify each choice.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) A sector graph, because each sector shows one category’s share of the whole budget. A divided bar graph is also suitable.

(b) A column graph, because the column heights show the actual amounts and make the categories easy to compare.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student joins points with straight lines to display classmates’ favourite fruits. The horizontal axis lists apple, banana, mango and pear; the vertical axis shows the number of students.
Explain why joining the points is unsuitable and name a better graph.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Favourite fruit is categorical data. A position between apple and banana has no meaning for this variable, so the joining lines suggest a change that the data does not represent.

A column graph is more suitable because separate columns compare the numbers choosing each fruit.

workedExamples.question_text:
Students record the number of times they visit the school library in a week. The results are whole-number counts.
The school wants to show the shape of the frequency distribution rather than each count’s percentage of the total.
Choose between a histogram and a sector graph, and justify your choice.
workedExamples.solution_text: A histogram. The number of visits is numerical discrete data, and a histogram shows how the frequencies are distributed along a numerical axis. A sector graph emphasises shares of a whole.

foundation.question_text:
A scientist measures a seedling’s height at the end of each day for two weeks and wants to show how the height changes over the fortnight.
Which type of graph is most suitable?
foundation.solution_text:
The purpose is to show change over time with continuous data.
A line graph is most suitable.

foundation.question_text:
A shop counts how many of each ice-cream flavour it sold and wants to compare the flavours.
Which type of graph is most suitable?
foundation.solution_text:
The data is categorical and the purpose is to compare categories.
A column (bar) graph is most suitable.

foundation.question_text:
You want to show what share of a monthly budget goes to rent, food and transport, out of the whole budget.
Which type of graph is most suitable?
foundation.solution_text:
The purpose is to show parts of a whole.
A sector (pie) graph is most suitable.

foundation.question_text:
A gardener records a sunflower’s height every week for $8$ weeks and wants to show how its height changes over time.
Which type of graph is most suitable?
foundation.solution_text:
Height is continuous numerical data and the purpose is to show change over time.
A line graph is most suitable.

foundation.question_text: Explain why a line graph is a suitable choice for showing a city’s temperature measured every hour through the day.
foundation.solution_text:
Temperature over time is continuous data that changes over time.
A line graph shows that change and lets you estimate values between the readings.

development.question_text:
A canteen wants a display showing the actual number of each drink sold this week, not the percentages.
Column graph or sector graph?
Justify your choice.
development.solution_text:
A sector graph primarily shows proportions of a whole; the total number sold is needed to recover the actual counts.
Choose a column graph, because it shows the actual number sold for each drink and makes them easy to compare.

Favourite sport is categorical data.
A line graph joins points to show change between them, but there is nothing between "soccer" and "netball", so a column graph should be used instead.

development.question_text:
A community centre records its annual spending on staff, equipment, building costs and activities. It wants to show each category’s share of the total spending.
Which type of graph is most suitable, and why?
development.solution_text:
A sector graph is most suitable, because each sector shows one spending category’s proportion of the whole.
A divided bar graph would also show these shares of the total.

development.question_text:
A charity wants a single display that shows how its total spending is split between four programs, as a share of the whole.
Which type of graph is most suitable, and why?
development.solution_text:
The purpose is to show parts of a whole.
A sector graph is most suitable, because each sector shows one program’s share of the total spending.

mastery.question_text:
A café has its total sales for each month of the year.
Name the most suitable graph for each purpose below and justify each choice.
(a) To show the trend in sales across the year.
(b) To show each month’s sales as a share of the year’s total.
mastery.solution_text:
(a) A line graph, because it shows change over time across the year.
(b) A sector graph, because it shows each month as a part of the whole year’s sales.

Car colours are unordered categories. The joining lines suggest values between the categories, but a position halfway between "Red" and "Blue" has no meaning for this data.
A column graph is a better display because separate columns make the numbers of cars in each colour easy to compare.
